Overview

The ambition.

A deep bank of assets that fuel LinkedIn, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts for months, not just a one-off recap. Content that feels real and human, moments that stop someone mid-scroll, client voices, client faces, names and logos front and centre.

Built to last months

A single event turned into a running content bank, not a one-off recap that's forgotten by October.

People, not just a stage

Not just Venus — client testimonials, their experience on the day, and how EZRA is changing the culture inside their own companies get equal weight.

A different shape this time

The main recap gets a new structure, see The Creative below, rather than repeating the last event's format.

Day One

Wed 16 Sept — New Office Opening.

An intimate evening: Venus Williams meeting a cohort of young early-career professionals from We Are Arrival at EZRA's brand-new London office. Candid, warm, emotionally rich, ribbon-cutting for the new Venus Room, GoC talent, VIP clients and EZRAnauts in the room.

Timings below reflect what's been discussed on calls so far, final timings to come from EZRA.

Crew arrive
1:00pm
Filming
4:00pm – 6:00pm
Guests / event
4:00pm – 6:30pm

What we capture

Venus meeting participants and clients, unguarded moments of connection. Participant reactions and room energy. B-roll of the new office, branding and atmosphere. Standalone moments for social clips. General GVs of the working office and the ribbon-cutting itself.

Crew & approach

Two cameras plus boom, a few key people mic'd rather than the whole room. Observational, reality-style shooting, directed remotely off monitors to keep a low profile. Steadicam pass on the space for extra B-roll.

Day Two

Thu 17 Sept — Main Event.

Full-day coverage, everything covered across five cameras, four fixed plus a roaming Steadicam, vision-mixed live to screens, sound fed direct from Gurps. Priority hierarchy: Venus/GoC moment first, client testimonials second, everything else third.

FILM
The Film
This style guide explains how we tend to film and edit the hero film with Venus Williams.

Hero Film Style Guide.

Not a highlights reel with testimonials bolted on the front. One hero film, for her and for the room EZRA built to hold her.

01
Arrival & Build

Venus opens the film. Before a single other frame, we hear her voice — then we see her, arriving across a dozen angles at once, all of it slow motion. Cut against her: chairs going out, the event space taking shape, guests starting to arrive. The two threads build side by side, crescendo together, and land on one big moment — that's where the film carries on.

Reference — cutting style, not audio
Arrival sequence from The Thomas Crown Affair

Shows the arrival treatment we're after. In the final edit this intercuts with the day's setup rather than running standalone like this.

Reference — not the event, just the energy
Setup: the hustle and bustle

Chairs and tables going out, monitors and equipment being unpacked, signage going up, people milling about and arriving — this is what gets intercut against her arrival, not this specific event.

The three beats below are examples of how this arrival could play out — not a fixed shot list.

02
The Approach
We hear her before we see the room
Click to expand+
Venus's voice, first

Before we see a single frame, we hear her. Venus opens the film in her own voice, then we watch her arrive — a dozen angles, all slow motion.

Not a montage — the real build

No generic highlight reel underneath her. The actual work of the day landing: chairs going out, the event space taking shape, guests starting to arrive.

One crescendo, one landing

Arrival and build crescendo together toward a single moment — then it lands, and the main film carries on from there.

03
Convergence
The two threads meet
Click to expand+
Cutting rhythm accelerates

The arrival cuts and the room-build cuts speed up against each other.

Two beats collide

Venus walking in, and the room arriving and settling down, both hearing her voice. She says something poignant, we land on her on stage — and it takes off from there.

04
Eruption
The room detonates the moment she lands
Click to expand+
The drop

The track drops the second she hits the stage.

Everything, full volume

Fireside energy, the GoC moment, testimonials, earned rather than front-loaded.

05
Graphics
Words locked to her, not floating over her
Click to expand+
Reference — technique only, not the look
Anchored graphics example

Ignore the typeface and colour here — this just shows the anchoring technique: graphics tracking a moving shot. We won't run graphics on screen throughout; certain words and phrases will pop up anchored to the movement, to keep it feeling dynamic.

Anchored, not constant

Graphics anchor specific words and phrases to a moving shot — brought up at chosen moments, not locked on screen throughout, to keep it feeling dynamic and exciting.

EZRA's own voice

The above is a reference to their typeface. We'll of course be using Be Vietnam Pro, EZRA's bold typeface, in EZRA Yellow.

Venus, and the event

This is built for Venus and the event. Every shot will be bespoke made with this graphic.
